title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 111 (Circulation of members' resolution)

content.overview: Section 111 requires a company, on a written requisition of such number of members as is required under section 100, to (a) give notice to members of any resolution which may properly be moved and is intended to be moved at a meeting, and (b) circulate to members any statement with respect to the matters referred to in the proposed resolution or the business to be dealt with at that meeting. The company is not bound to do so unless the requisition is deposited in time with a sum reasonably sufficient for expenses; it need not circulate a statement if the Central Government declares the right is being abused to secure needless publicity for defamatory matter. Default attracts a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees on the company and every officer in default.
content.glance: On a valid members' requisition (same strength as section 100), the company must give notice of a properly movable resolution or circulate a members' statement, subject to deposit, timing and the defamatory-matter safeguard.
content.study:
## Section 111 — circulation of members' resolution

**Subsection (1): duty on requisition.** A company shall, on requisition in writing of such number of members as required in section 100,—
- (a) give notice to members of any resolution which may properly be moved and is intended to be moved at a meeting; and
- (b) circulate to members any statement with respect to the matters referred to in the proposed resolution or the business to be dealt with at that meeting.

**Subsection (2): conditions.** The company is not bound under this section to give notice of any resolution or to circulate any statement unless—
- (a) a copy of the requisition signed by the requisitionists (or two or more copies which between them contain the signatures of all the requisitionists) is deposited at the registered office—
  - (i) for a requisition requiring notice of a resolution: not less than six weeks before the meeting;
  - (ii) for any other requisition: not less than two weeks before the meeting; and
- (b) there is deposited or tendered with the requisition a sum reasonably sufficient to meet the company's expenses in giving effect thereto.

**Proviso to subsection (2).** If after a requisition requiring notice of a resolution is deposited an AGM is called on a date within six weeks after deposit, the copy is deemed properly deposited even if not deposited within the six-week period.

**Subsection (3): defamatory matter.** The company is not bound to circulate any statement under clause (b) of subsection (1) if, on the application of the company or any other person who claims to be aggrieved, the Central Government by order declares that the rights conferred by this section are being abused to secure needless publicity for defamatory matter.

**Subsection (4): costs.** An order under subsection (3) may also direct that the cost incurred by the company by virtue of this section shall be paid to the company by the requisitionists, even if they are not parties to the application.

**Subsection (5): penalty.** If any default is made in complying with this section, the company and every officer of the company who is in default shall be liable to a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees.

## Apply the provision
- Confirm the requisition strength under section 100, deposit timing, and expense deposit.
- Distinguish notice of a resolution (six weeks) from circulation of a statement (two weeks).
- Check whether a Central Government order under subsection (3) has displaced the duty to circulate a statement.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Subsection (1): notice and circulation on requisition
sections.body: On a written requisition of the number of members required under section 100, the company must give notice of a resolution that may properly be moved and is intended to be moved, and circulate a statement on the matters in the proposed resolution or business.

sections.heading: Subsection (2): deposit timing and expenses
sections.body: The company is not bound unless the signed requisition is deposited at the registered office (six weeks for notice of a resolution; two weeks for other requisitions) with a sum reasonably sufficient for expenses. An AGM called within six weeks after deposit of a resolution requisition deems the deposit timely.

sections.heading: Subsections (3)–(5): defamatory safeguard, costs and penalty
sections.body: The Central Government may declare that circulation is being abused for needless publicity of defamatory matter. Costs may be ordered against the requisitionists. Default attracts a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees on the company and every officer in default.

provisions.title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 111 (Circulation of members' resolution)

examples.title: Valid requisition for notice of a resolution
examples.body: Members meeting the section 100 threshold deposit a signed requisition for notice of a resolution at the registered office more than six weeks before the meeting, with a sum reasonably sufficient for expenses. The company must give notice of the resolution if it may properly be moved and is intended to be moved. This is an educational illustration.

examples.title: Defamatory-matter order
examples.body: The company applies to the Central Government under subsection (3). The Government declares that the right is being abused to secure needless publicity for defamatory matter. The company is not bound to circulate the statement. This is an educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: A requisition requiring notice of a resolution is deposited four weeks before the meeting. Is the company bound under section 111(2)?
hypotheticals.analysis: No, unless the proviso applies. For a requisition requiring notice of a resolution the deposit must be not less than six weeks before the meeting. Four weeks is insufficient. If an AGM is called on a date within six weeks after the deposit, the proviso may deem the deposit timely.

hypotheticals.question: Who may apply for a Central Government order under subsection (3)?
hypotheticals.analysis: Either the company or any other person who claims to be aggrieved may apply. The order declares that the rights are being abused to secure needless publicity for defamatory matter.

misconceptions.trap: Treating any members' request as sufficient without the section 100 strength and timely deposit.
misconceptions.correction: The requisition must meet the section 100 number and the subsection (2) deposit and expense conditions.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the company can refuse circulation for any reason it considers inconvenient.
misconceptions.correction: Refusal to circulate a statement under clause (b) requires a Central Government order under subsection (3) on the defamatory-matter ground.

misconceptions.trap: Confusing the six-week and two-week deposit periods.
misconceptions.correction: Six weeks applies to a requisition requiring notice of a resolution; two weeks applies to any other requisition.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 111 require?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: On a valid written requisition of the number of members required under section 100, the company must give notice of a properly movable resolution intended to be moved, or circulate a statement on the matters in the proposed resolution or business, subject to deposit timing, expense deposit, and the Central Government's power to stop circulation of defamatory matter. Default attracts a penalty of twenty-five thousand rupees.
